# Rage on Crit {#rage-on-crit}

```{r setup-crit, include=FALSE}
# Reuses `conv`, `classic_k`, the Forever rates (`forever_mh`, `forever_oh`, `forever_draws`) and the fight simulator
# from the Rage Generation chapter, and `ladder` from the How Damage Scales chapter. The chapter is about today's game
# (the 2 Nov build). The older rule versions (v0, v1, v2 on the 1 Oct build) are still simulated here, because Classic
# comes from the same saved grid and How the Rules Changed uses the versions.
source("data/sim_cache.R")
source("data/wowsims.R")   # today's game is simmed in wowsims (see SIMS.md)
library(parallel)

crit_changelog <- tribble(
  ~version, ~date,        ~change,
  "4.0.2",  "2026-11-19", "Wording: the gear phases are modeled on what warriors wore in Classic, since Forever's gear isn't known yet, so the chapter now says phase 2-like gear (and so on) instead of phase 2. No numbers change.",
  "4.0.1",  "2026-11-18", "Correction: glancing blows do 65% damage on average in Forever (a roll between 55% and 75% in wowsims), the same as Classic. Version 4.0.0 wrongly said 70%.",
  "4.0.0",  "2026-11-18", "Today's game is now simmed in wowsims (github.com/wowsims/forever), the community simulator, which the book follows as the source of truth: every rage map, the Heroic Strike waits and the gear-point table for today's Forever. The attack table follows wowsims for every set of rules: a boss three levels up takes 4.8% off your crit (the chapter used to assume no crit suppression). Classic, the older versions and the no-crit-bonus line stay on our simulator, a simplified model.",
  "3.0.0",  "2026-11-17", "Rebuilt on today's game (the 2 Nov build: crits x2, off hand x1.5, Flurry 30%, Improved Whirlwind and Reckless Swings) against Classic, at every crit, hit and attack power, with today's game without the crit bonus to show what the rule adds. The comparison of the rule versions (v0, v1 and v2 on the 1 Oct build) moved to How the Rules Changed, and the two design ideas were taken out. The check against Bored's spreadsheet stays.",
  "2.1.0",  "2026-11-04", "Added Since 2 November: Blizzard's 2 Nov notes gave Fury Flurry 3/3 at 30%, Improved Whirlwind and Reckless Swings. The crit rules are unchanged, so the versions stay on the build they were announced for (1 Oct to 2 Nov), and today's game is simulated alongside them at every crit and hit.",
  "2.0.0",  "2026-10-28", "v2 is in the game: Blizzard's 1 Oct development notes give crits 100% more rage, and the hotfixed talent tree gives Dual Wield Specialization +50% off-hand rage, with its off-hand hit moved to Furious Precision. The rest of the book now uses v2. Every version is simulated on today's build otherwise (Bloodthirst at 45% of attack power, a 100 rage cap without Boundless Rage, Whirlwind for 22 rage with Raging Blows, and a queued Heroic Strike no longer raising off-hand hit), and the rage Bloodthirst and Whirlwind need comes from the How Damage Scales chapter's rage blocks.",
  "1.0.0",  "2026-10-01", "First version: three versions of Forever's rage (v0 before 30 September; v1, the 30 September change, where crits give 75% more rage and Dual Wield Specialization no longer adds off-hand rage; and v2, the fix Zirene announced, where crits give 100% more and the off hand 50% more) against Classic, at every crit, hit and attack power. Where the ceiling comes from, how long you wait between Heroic Strikes, an interactive map for your own gear, a check against Bored's rage spreadsheet, and two design ideas."
)

C60 <- conv(60)
crit_wpn <- 58   # the phase 2-like weapon from the How Damage Scales chapter, held fixed
# The attack table against a level 63 boss with 300 weapon skill, as wowsims has it: 27% white miss for a dual wielder
# and 8% for abilities before hit from gear, 6.5% dodge, 40% glancing blows (a 55% to 75% damage roll in wowsims, 65%
# on average, as in Classic), and the boss takes 4.8% off your crit (sim_defaults$crit_suppression). Windfury Totem is
# always up.
crit_table <- function(hit) list(miss = 0.27 - hit, yellow_miss = max(0.08 - hit, 0),
                                 dodge = 0.065, glance = 0.40, wf = TRUE)
# Each version of the rage rules. Forever versions use the 17/34/0 Forever build as it was from 1 Oct to 2 Nov
# (`forever_oct_talents`: Bloodthirst at 45%, a 100 rage cap, Whirlwind for 22 rage, Flurry 25%); only the off-hand
# rage multiplier (Dual Wield Specialization), the crit multiplier and the Flurry bonus change, so the versions differ
# in their rage and nothing else. `Forever today` is v2 on the 2 Nov build (`forever_talents`: Flurry 30%, Improved
# Whirlwind, Reckless Swings), for the "Since 2 November" section.
#   v0: before 30 Sep 2026 (off hand x2, no crit bonus)
#   v1: the 30 Sep change (crits x1.75, off hand x1)
#   v2: the game since the 1 to 2 Oct hotfixes, as Zirene announced (crits x2, off hand x1.5)
crit_versions <- list(
  `Forever v0`             = list(game = "Forever", p = list(oh_rage_mult = 2, crit_rage_mult = 1)),
  `Off hand x1, no crit bonus` = list(game = "Forever", p = list(oh_rage_mult = 1, crit_rage_mult = 1)),
  `Forever v1`                = list(game = "Forever", p = list(oh_rage_mult = 1, crit_rage_mult = 1.75)),
  `Forever v2`                 = list(game = "Forever", p = list(oh_rage_mult = 1.5, crit_rage_mult = 2)),
  `Classic`                    = list(game = "Classic", p = list()),
  `Crits x2, off hand x2`      = list(game = "Forever", p = list(oh_rage_mult = 2, crit_rage_mult = 2)),
  `Flurry +1`                  = list(game = "Forever", p = list(oh_rage_mult = 1, crit_rage_mult = 1, flurry_rage = 1)),
  `Flurry +2`                  = list(game = "Forever", p = list(oh_rage_mult = 1, crit_rage_mult = 1, flurry_rage = 2)),
  `Flurry +3`                  = list(game = "Forever", p = list(oh_rage_mult = 1, crit_rage_mult = 1, flurry_rage = 3)),
  `Flurry +4`                  = list(game = "Forever", p = list(oh_rage_mult = 1, crit_rage_mult = 1, flurry_rage = 4)),
  `Flurry +5`                  = list(game = "Forever", p = list(oh_rage_mult = 1, crit_rage_mult = 1, flurry_rage = 5)),
  `Forever today`              = list(game = "Forever", p = list(), now = TRUE)
)
# Gear: every combination of attack power, crit (character sheet) and hit from gear. Forever's rage doesn't use
# damage, so the design options only run at 2000 attack power; the three main versions run everywhere, to show it.
full_ap  <- c("Forever v0", "Forever v1", "Forever v2", "Classic")
main_models <- full_ap   # the four versions most figures compare
crit_grid <- bind_rows(
  expand_grid(model = full_ap, ap = seq(1000, 3000, 250), crit = seq(0.15, 0.45, 0.05), hit = seq(0, 0.15, 0.025)),
  expand_grid(model = setdiff(names(crit_versions), full_ap), ap = 2000, crit = seq(0.15, 0.45, 0.05), hit = seq(0, 0.15, 0.025))
) %>% mutate(across(c(crit, hit), ~ round(.x, 3)))
# Three gear points, for the closer looks
gear_points <- tribble(~point, ~ap, ~crit, ~hit,
  "Early", 1250, 0.20, 0.05,
  "Mid",   2000, 0.30, 0.075,
  "Late",  2750, 0.40, 0.10)
n_crit <- 60; crit_fight_len <- 600   # fights per gear point, and their length (long, so the opening matters little)
# rage per second Bloodthirst and Whirlwind use when cast on cooldown (the How Damage Scales chapter's rage blocks),
# on the 1 Oct build (Whirlwind every 10 sec, about 5 a minute) and today's (Improved Whirlwind)
bt_ww_need     <- round(ladder("Forever", crit_wpn, ww_pm = ww_per_min[["Classic"]], tal = forever_oct_talents)$blocks$end[2], 1)
bt_ww_need_now <- round(ladder("Forever", crit_wpn)$blocks$end[2], 1)
```

```{r crit-sims, include=FALSE}
# functions go into the key as their code (deparse), so where the chapter sits in the merged book doesn't change it
crit_res <- cached_sim("crit_grid", deps = list(crit_grid, crit_versions, deparse(crit_table), gear_points, n_crit, crit_fight_len, crit_wpn, classic_k, forever_draws, C60, sim_defaults, forever_talents, forever_oct_talents, classic_talents), {
  cl <- makeCluster(max(1, min(14, detectCores() - 2)))
  on.exit(stopCluster(cl))
  clusterCall(cl, setwd, getwd())
  clusterExport(cl, c("crit_versions", "crit_table", "gear_points", "n_crit", "crit_fight_len", "crit_wpn", "classic_k", "forever_draws", "C60", "full_ap"), envir = environment())
  invisible(clusterEvalQ(cl, { suppressMessages(library(tidyverse)); source("data/fight_sim.R") }))
  rows <- split(crit_grid, seq_len(nrow(crit_grid)))
  bind_rows(parLapplyLB(cl, rows, function(j) {
    v <- crit_versions[[j$model]]
    talents <- if (v$game == "Classic") classic_talents else if (isTRUE(v$now)) forever_talents else forever_oct_talents
    p <- modifyList(modifyList(modifyList(sim_defaults, talents), crit_table(j$hit)),
                    c(list(ap = j$ap, crit = j$crit, fight_len = crit_fight_len), v$p))
    rage_fn <- if (v$game == "Classic") function(hand, dmg, speed) classic_k * dmg / C60
               else function(hand, dmg, speed) sample(forever_draws[[hand]], 1) * speed
    r <- map_dfr(seq_len(n_crit), function(i) { set.seed(900 + i); simulate_fight(rage_fn, crit_wpn, p) })
    gaps <- unlist(lapply(r$hs_t, diff))   # seconds between one Heroic Strike and the next
    # keep every gap only at the three gear points (Forever's options stand in at any attack power)
    keep <- any(abs(gear_points$crit - j$crit) < 1e-9 & abs(gear_points$hit - j$hit) < 1e-9 &
                (gear_points$ap == j$ap | !(j$model %in% full_ap)))
    tibble(j, rps = mean(r$rps), dps = mean(r$total_dps), bt = mean(r$bt_pm), ww = mean(r$ww_pm), hs = mean(r$hs_pm),
           starved = mean(r$starved_share), wasted = mean(r$wasted_pm),
           gap_med = median(gaps), gap_p90 = unname(quantile(gaps, 0.9)), gaps = list(if (keep) gaps else NULL))
  }))
})

# Bored's spreadsheet (75% Crit Rage Mod tab), and our simulator with its assumptions swapped for ours one at a time
sheet_rows <- tribble(~row, ~hit, ~exp, ~crit, ~sheet_rps,
  "No hit, 25% crit",                 0.00, 0.00, 0.25, 6.355,
  "9% hit, 30% crit",                 0.09, 0.00, 0.30, 7.398,
  "12% hit, 6% expertise, 40% crit",  0.12, 0.06, 0.40, 8.727,
  "18% hit, 6% expertise, 45% crit",  0.18, 0.06, 0.45, 9.551)
sheet_steps <- list(
  `Our simulator, the sheet's assumptions, no Heroic Strike` = function(r) list(hs_threshold = 1e6),
  `... with Heroic Strike` = function(r) list(),
  `... Windfury with a 1.5 sec cooldown` = function(r) list(wf_icd = 1.5),
  `... no extra 3% attack speed` = function(r) list(wf_icd = 1.5, extra_haste = 1),
  `... our miss table` = function(r) list(wf_icd = 1.5, extra_haste = 1, miss = 0.27 - r$hit, yellow_miss = max(0.08 - r$hit, 0), dodge = 0.065 - r$exp),
  `... Anger Management` = function(r) list(wf_icd = 1.5, extra_haste = 1, miss = 0.27 - r$hit, yellow_miss = max(0.08 - r$hit, 0), dodge = 0.065 - r$exp, anger_rps = 1 / 3),
  `... a 2.0 speed off hand (our assumptions)` = function(r) list(wf_icd = 1.5, extra_haste = 1, miss = 0.27 - r$hit, yellow_miss = max(0.08 - r$hit, 0), dodge = 0.065 - r$exp, anger_rps = 1 / 3, oh_speed = 2.0)
)
sheet_res <- cached_sim("crit_sheet", deps = list(sheet_rows, lapply(sheet_steps, deparse), sim_defaults, forever_oct_talents), {
  fixed_rates <- function(hand, dmg, speed) (if (hand == "MH") 3.46 else 1.73) * speed   # the sheet's base rage values
  expand_grid(i = seq_len(nrow(sheet_rows)), step = names(sheet_steps)) %>%
    mutate(rps = map2_dbl(i, step, function(ii, s) {
      r <- sheet_rows[ii, ]
      # the sheet: tooltip misses (27.6% / 8.6% before hit), 6.6% dodge, no crit suppression, Windfury on every
      # attack, 3% attack speed from enchants, a 2.7 speed off hand, no Anger Management
      p <- modifyList(modifyList(sim_defaults, forever_oct_talents),   # the build the spreadsheet models
                      list(miss = 0.276 - r$hit, yellow_miss = max(0.086 - r$hit, 0), dodge = 0.066 - r$exp, crit = r$crit,
                           crit_suppression = 0, anger_rps = 0, wf = TRUE, wf_icd = 0, extra_haste = 1.03, oh_speed = 2.7,
                           oh_rage_mult = 1, crit_rage_mult = 1.75, ap = 1300, fight_len = 600))
      p <- modifyList(p, sheet_steps[[s]](r))
      mean(map_dbl(1:60, function(k) { set.seed(900 + k); simulate_fight(fixed_rates, 58, p)$rps }))
    })) %>% mutate(row = sheet_rows$row[i])
})

# Today's game (the 2 Nov build, `forever_talents`) at every attack power, crit and hit, and the same game without the
# crit bonus. Forever's rage doesn't use damage, so the no-bonus game only runs at 2000 attack power. Classic comes
# from the grid above.
now_versions <- list(
  `Forever`                = list(p = list()),
  `Forever, no crit bonus` = list(p = list(crit_rage_mult = 1))
)
now_grid <- bind_rows(
  expand_grid(model = "Forever", ap = seq(1000, 3000, 250), crit = seq(0.15, 0.45, 0.05), hit = seq(0, 0.15, 0.025)),
  expand_grid(model = "Forever, no crit bonus", ap = 2000, crit = seq(0.15, 0.45, 0.05), hit = seq(0, 0.15, 0.025))
) %>% mutate(across(c(crit, hit), ~ round(.x, 3)))
# Today's Forever in wowsims: every cell of the grid, 30 ten-minute fights each, fight by fight so the Heroic Strike
# waits come from the combat logs. The no-crit-bonus game can't be run in wowsims, so it stays on our simulator.
n_crit_ws <- 30
now_ws_grid <- filter(now_grid, model == "Forever")
now_ws_setups <- setNames(pmap(now_ws_grid, function(model, ap, crit, hit) {
  book_wowsims(crit_wpn, ap, crit, hit, p = list(raid_buffs = "windfury_totem", duration = crit_fight_len))
}), paste(now_ws_grid$ap, now_ws_grid$crit, now_ws_grid$hit, sep = "|"))
now_ws_fights <- wowsims_fights("crit_grid_now", now_ws_setups, n_crit_ws, seed0 = 900)
crit_ws_stamp <- wowsims_stamp(list(version = attr(now_ws_fights, "version")))
crit_res_now_ws <- now_ws_fights %>%
  separate(setup, c("ap", "crit", "hit"), sep = "\\|", convert = TRUE) %>%
  group_by(ap, crit, hit) %>%
  summarise(rps = mean(rps), dps = mean(total_dps), bt = mean(bt_pm), ww = mean(ww_pm), hs = mean(hs_pm),
            starved = mean(starved_share), wasted = NA_real_, gaps = list(unlist(lapply(hs_t, diff))), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(model = "Forever", gap_med = map_dbl(gaps, median), gap_p90 = map_dbl(gaps, ~ unname(quantile(.x, 0.9))),
         keep = pmap_lgl(list(ap, crit, hit), function(a, c, h)
           any(abs(gear_points$crit - c) < 1e-9 & abs(gear_points$hit - h) < 1e-9 & gear_points$ap == a)),
         gaps = map2(gaps, keep, ~ if (.y) .x else NULL)) %>%
  select(-keep)
crit_res_now_nb <- cached_sim("crit_grid_now", deps = list(filter(now_grid, model != "Forever"), now_versions, deparse(crit_table), gear_points, n_crit, crit_fight_len, crit_wpn, forever_draws, sim_defaults, forever_talents), {
  cl <- makeCluster(max(1, min(14, detectCores() - 2)))
  on.exit(stopCluster(cl))
  clusterCall(cl, setwd, getwd())
  clusterExport(cl, c("now_versions", "crit_table", "gear_points", "n_crit", "crit_fight_len", "crit_wpn", "forever_draws"), envir = environment())
  invisible(clusterEvalQ(cl, { suppressMessages(library(tidyverse)); source("data/fight_sim.R") }))
  rows <- split(filter(now_grid, model != "Forever"), seq_len(sum(now_grid$model != "Forever")))
  bind_rows(parLapplyLB(cl, rows, function(j) {
    p <- modifyList(modifyList(modifyList(sim_defaults, forever_talents), crit_table(j$hit)),
                    c(list(ap = j$ap, crit = j$crit, fight_len = crit_fight_len), now_versions[[j$model]]$p))
    rage_fn <- function(hand, dmg, speed) sample(forever_draws[[hand]], 1) * speed
    r <- map_dfr(seq_len(n_crit), function(i) { set.seed(900 + i); simulate_fight(rage_fn, crit_wpn, p) })
    gaps <- unlist(lapply(r$hs_t, diff))   # seconds between one Heroic Strike and the next
    # keep every gap only at the three gear points (the no-bonus game stands in at any attack power)
    keep <- any(abs(gear_points$crit - j$crit) < 1e-9 & abs(gear_points$hit - j$hit) < 1e-9)
    tibble(j, rps = mean(r$rps), dps = mean(r$total_dps), bt = mean(r$bt_pm), ww = mean(r$ww_pm), hs = mean(r$hs_pm),
           starved = mean(r$starved_share), wasted = mean(r$wasted_pm),
           gap_med = median(gaps), gap_p90 = unname(quantile(gaps, 0.9)), gaps = list(if (keep) gaps else NULL))
  }))
})
crit_res_now <- bind_rows(crit_res_now_ws, crit_res_now_nb)
```

```{r crit-helpers, include=FALSE}
crit_res <- crit_res %>% mutate(across(c(crit, hit), ~ round(.x, 3)))
# Every simulated set of rules in one table: today's game, Classic, and the older rule versions (for How the Rules Changed)
crit_all <- bind_rows(crit_res, crit_res_now) %>% mutate(across(c(crit, hit), ~ round(.x, 3)))
main_models <- c("Forever", "Classic")   # the two sets of rules most figures compare
# One value from the grid. Only Classic and today's Forever were run at every attack power; Forever's rage doesn't
# depend on it, so the other Forever rules are read at 2000.
gv <- function(model, crit, hit, ap = 2000, col = "rps") {
  if (!(model %in% c("Classic", "Forever"))) ap <- 2000
  x <- crit_all[[col]][crit_all$model == model & crit_all$ap == ap & abs(crit_all$crit - crit) < 1e-9 & abs(crit_all$hit - hit) < 1e-9]
  stopifnot(length(x) == 1); x
}
f2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x); f1 <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x); f0 <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f", x)
pc  <- function(x) paste0(round(x * 100, 1), "%")   # 6.5%, 27%
pc0 <- function(x) paste0(round(x * 100), "%")
gp <- split(gear_points, gear_points$point)[gear_points$point]
at_point <- function(model, pt, col = "rps") with(gp[[pt]], gv(model, crit, hit, ap, col))
gear_label <- function(pt) with(gp[[pt]], sprintf("%s: %d AP, %s crit, %s hit", pt, ap, pc(crit), pc(hit)))
# Every gap between Heroic Strikes at a gear point
gaps_at <- function(model, pt) {
  g <- gp[[pt]]; a <- if (model %in% c("Classic", "Forever")) g$ap else 2000
  crit_all$gaps[crit_all$model == model & crit_all$ap == a & abs(crit_all$crit - g$crit) < 1e-9 & abs(crit_all$hit - g$hit) < 1e-9][[1]]
}
# The crit you need for Bloodthirst + Whirlwind at a given hit (not used now that every gear covers it; kept for checks) (at 2000 attack power)
crit_needed <- function(model, hit, need = bt_ww_need_now) {
  d <- crit_all %>% filter(model == !!model, ap == 2000, abs(hit - !!hit) < 1e-9) %>% arrange(crit)
  if (min(d$rps) >= need) return("under 15%")
  if (max(d$rps) < need) return("over 45%")
  pc0(approx(d$rps, d$crit, xout = need, ties = "ordered")$y)
}
# The crit where a version's crit bonus gives back the off-hand rage it took away, against v0 (How the Rules Changed):
# oh is the version's off-hand multiplier, bonus its crit bonus (m - 1)
be_crit <- function(oh, bonus, hit = 0.075) {
  land_oh <- 1 - max(0.27 - hit - forever_talents$oh_hit_bonus, 0) - 0.065
  (2 - oh) * forever_oh * land_oh / (bonus * (forever_mh + oh * forever_oh))
}
v2_gain <- crit_res %>% filter(ap == 2000, model %in% c("Forever v0", "Forever v2")) %>% select(model, crit, hit, rps) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = rps) %>% with(range(`Forever v2` - `Forever v0`))
# The most crit a swing can have: whatever is left of the attack table after misses, dodges and glancing blows
crit_cap <- function(hit, hand) 1 - pmax(0.27 - hit - (if (hand == "OH") forever_talents$oh_hit_bonus else 0), 0) - 0.065 - 0.40
# What the crit bonus adds to today's rage, across the grid at 2000 attack power
bonus_diff <- crit_all %>% filter(ap == 2000, model %in% c("Forever", "Forever, no crit bonus")) %>%
  select(model, crit, hit, rps) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = rps) %>%
  mutate(d = Forever - `Forever, no crit bonus`)

crit_cols <- c(`Forever` = "#08306b", `Forever, no crit bonus` = "#9ecae1", `Classic` = "grey45",
               `Classic (1250 AP)` = "grey70", `Classic (2000 AP)` = "grey45",
               `Forever v0` = "#9ecae1", `Forever v1` = "#4292c6", `Forever v2` = "#08306b")
crit_labs <- c(`Forever` = "Forever today\n(crits x2, off hand x1.5)", `Classic` = "Classic\n(7.5 x damage / C)",
               `Forever, no crit bonus` = "Forever today,\nno crit bonus")
blues <- c("#deebf7", "#c6dbef", "#9ecae1", "#6baed6", "#4292c6", "#2171b5", "#08519c", "#08306b")
# One continuous colour scale for every rage-per-second map, so the same colour means the same rage in each
rps_range <- range(crit_all$rps[crit_all$model %in% main_models])
rps_fill <- scale_fill_gradientn(colours = blues, limits = rps_range, name = "Rage per second",
                                 guide = guide_colourbar(barwidth = unit(14, "lines"), title.position = "top"))
# Interactive 3D view (plotly): one scene per set of rules, side by side like the maps. Crit and hit are on the floor,
# the value is the height and the colour, contour lines are projected onto the floor, and a slider sets attack power
# for both. Forever's surface doesn't change with attack power; Classic's does.
crit3d <- function(col, ztitle, colours, cmin, cmax, step, zcap = Inf, fmt = ".2f", unit = "") {
  ms <- main_models; n <- length(ms)
  scenes <- c("scene", paste0("scene", seq_len(n)[-1]))
  aps <- sort(unique(crit_all$ap[crit_all$model == "Classic"]))
  crits <- sort(unique(crit_all$crit)); hits <- sort(unique(crit_all$hit))
  cscale <- map2(seq(0, 1, length.out = length(colours)), colours, ~ list(.x, .y))
  p <- plotly::plot_ly()
  for (a in aps) for (k in seq_along(ms)) {
    d <- crit_all %>% filter(model == ms[k], ap == a) %>% transmute(crit, hit, v = pmin(.data[[col]], zcap))
    zm <- d %>% pivot_wider(names_from = crit, values_from = v) %>% arrange(hit) %>% select(as.character(crits)) %>% as.matrix()
    p <- p %>% plotly::add_surface(x = crits * 100, y = hits * 100, z = zm, scene = scenes[k], name = ms[k],
      colorscale = cscale, cmin = cmin, cmax = cmax, showscale = k == n, visible = a == 2000,
      colorbar = list(title = list(text = ztitle), len = 0.6, thickness = 14, y = 0.55, x = 0.93),
      contours = list(z = list(show = TRUE, start = cmin, end = cmax, size = step, color = "#525252", width = 1,
                               project = list(z = TRUE))),
      hovertemplate = paste0(ms[k], "<br>Crit %{x}%<br>Hit %{y}%<br>%{z:", fmt, "}", unit, "<extra></extra>"))
  }
  steps <- lapply(seq_along(aps), function(i) list(method = "restyle", label = as.character(aps[i]),
    args = list("visible", as.list(rep(seq_along(aps) == i, each = n)))))
  x0 <- (seq_len(n) - 1) * 0.46
  scene <- function(k) list(domain = list(x = c(x0[k], x0[k] + 0.44), y = c(0.14, 0.92)),
    xaxis = list(title = "Crit (%)"), yaxis = list(title = "Hit (%)"), zaxis = list(title = "", range = c(0, cmax * 1.05)),
    camera = list(eye = list(x = 1.6, y = -1.5, z = 0.8)), aspectmode = "manual", aspectratio = list(x = 1.2, y = 1, z = 0.7))
  titles <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(k) list(text = paste0("<b>", ms[k], "</b>"), x = x0[k] + 0.01, y = 1,
    xref = "paper", yref = "paper", showarrow = FALSE, xanchor = "left", yanchor = "top", font = list(size = 14)))
  do.call(plotly::layout, c(list(p), setNames(lapply(seq_len(n), scene), scenes),
    list(annotations = titles, showlegend = FALSE,
         sliders = list(list(active = which(aps == 2000) - 1, currentvalue = list(prefix = "Attack power: "), steps = steps,
                             y = 0.08, len = 0.88, pad = list(t = 10))),
         margin = list(l = 0, r = 0, t = 30, b = 0))))
}
# Interactive version of the crit x hit map, built in plotly so the sliders can drive both panels: the same colours,
# white steps of 0.5 rage per second, the dashed Bloodthirst + Whirlwind line and the 5-10% hit band.
map_models <- main_models
map_z <- function(m, ap = 2000) crit_all %>% filter(model == m, ap == !!ap) %>% transmute(crit, hit, rps) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = crit, values_from = rps) %>% arrange(hit) %>% select(-hit) %>% as.matrix()
map_axes <- function(n) list(x = c("x", paste0("x", seq_len(n)[-1])), y = c("y", paste0("y", seq_len(n)[-1])))
crit_map_base <- function(top = 1) {
  crits <- sort(unique(crit_all$crit)) * 100; hits <- sort(unique(crit_all$hit)) * 100
  cscale <- map2(seq(0, 1, length.out = length(blues)), blues, ~ list(.x, .y))
  n <- length(map_models); ax <- map_axes(n)
  p <- plotly::plot_ly()
  for (k in seq_len(n)) {
    zm <- map_z(map_models[k])
    p <- p %>%
      plotly::add_trace(type = "heatmap", x = crits, y = hits, z = zm, xaxis = ax$x[k], yaxis = ax$y[k],
        colorscale = cscale, zmin = rps_range[1], zmax = rps_range[2], zsmooth = "best", showscale = k == n,
        colorbar = list(title = list(text = "Rage per<br>second"), thickness = 14, len = 0.6, y = (top + 0.24) / 2),
        hovertemplate = paste0(map_models[k], "<br>Crit %{x}%<br>Hit %{y}%<br>%{z:.2f} rage per second<extra></extra>")) %>%
      plotly::add_trace(type = "contour", x = crits, y = hits, z = zm, xaxis = ax$x[k], yaxis = ax$y[k],
        contours = list(coloring = "none", start = 5, end = 14, size = 0.5), line = list(color = "white", width = 0.6),
        showscale = FALSE, hoverinfo = "skip")
  }
  dom <- list(c(0, 0.42), c(0.48, 0.90)); rows <- c(0.24, top - 0.06)
  xaxes <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(k) list(domain = dom[[k]], anchor = ax$y[k], title = "Crit (%)", range = range(crits)))
  yaxes <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(k) list(domain = rows, anchor = ax$x[k], title = if (k == 1) "Hit from gear (%)" else "",
                                               range = range(hits)))
  band <- function(xr, yr) lapply(c(5, 10), function(h) list(type = "line", xref = xr, yref = yr, x0 = min(crits), x1 = max(crits),
    y0 = h, y1 = h, line = list(color = "white", width = 1.5, dash = "dot")))
  titles <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(k) list(text = paste0("<b>", map_models[k], "</b>"), x = mean(dom[[k]]), y = rows[2],
    xref = "paper", yref = "paper", showarrow = FALSE, xanchor = "center", yanchor = "bottom"))
  do.call(plotly::layout, c(list(p),
    setNames(xaxes, c("xaxis", paste0("xaxis", seq_len(n)[-1]))), setNames(yaxes, c("yaxis", paste0("yaxis", seq_len(n)[-1]))),
    list(shapes = do.call(c, lapply(seq_len(n), function(k) band(ax$x[k], ax$y[k]))), annotations = titles, showlegend = FALSE,
         margin = list(l = 60, r = 10, t = 10, b = 10)))) %>%
    plotly::config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
}
# Crit and hit sliders move a marker to your gear on both maps, and a line above reads out your rage
crit_map_pick <- function(crit0 = 30, hit0 = 7.5) {
  crits <- sort(unique(crit_all$crit)) * 100; hits <- sort(unique(crit_all$hit)) * 100
  n <- length(map_models); ax <- map_axes(n)
  p <- crit_map_base(top = 0.88)
  for (k in seq_len(n)) p <- p %>% plotly::add_trace(type = "scatter", mode = "markers", x = crit0, y = hit0,
    xaxis = ax$x[k], yaxis = ax$y[k], hoverinfo = "skip",
    marker = list(symbol = "circle-open", size = 18, color = "#d7301f", line = list(width = 3)))
  steps <- function(v) lapply(v, function(x) list(method = "skip", label = as.character(x), args = list()))
  # plotly adds this to the panel titles already in the layout; the readout is the last one, which the script below fills in
  ann <- list(list(text = "", x = 0, y = 1, xref = "paper", yref = "paper", showarrow = FALSE,
    xanchor = "left", yanchor = "top", align = "left", font = list(size = 13)))
  p <- p %>% plotly::layout(annotations = ann, sliders = list(
    list(active = which(crits == crit0) - 1, currentvalue = list(prefix = "Crit: ", suffix = "%"), steps = steps(crits),
         x = 0, len = 0.43, y = 0.09, pad = list(t = 0)),
    list(active = which(abs(hits - hit0) < 1e-9) - 1, currentvalue = list(prefix = "Hit from gear: ", suffix = "%"), steps = steps(hits),
         x = 0.48, len = 0.43, y = 0.09, pad = list(t = 0))))
  htmlwidgets::onRender(p, "
    function(el, x, d) {
      var state = {c: d.c0, h: d.h0};
      function update() {
        var ci = d.crits.indexOf(state.c), hi = d.hits.indexOf(state.h);
        var parts = d.models.map(function(m, k) {
          var v = d.z[k][hi][ci];
          return m + ' <b>' + v.toFixed(2) + '</b>';
        });
        var ann = el.layout.annotations.slice();
        ann[ann.length - 1] = Object.assign({}, ann[ann.length - 1], {text: '<b>Your rage per second</b> at ' + state.c + '% crit and ' + state.h + '% hit<br>' +
          parts.join(' &#183; ')});
        var xs = d.markers.map(function() { return [state.c]; }), ys = d.markers.map(function() { return [state.h]; });
        Plotly.update(el, {x: xs, y: ys}, {annotations: ann}, d.markers);
      }
      el.on('plotly_sliderchange', function(e) {
        var v = parseFloat(e.step.label);
        if (e.slider._index === 0) state.c = v; else state.h = v;
        update();
      });
      update();
    }", data = list(c0 = crit0, h0 = hit0, crits = crits, hits = hits, models = map_models,
                    z = lapply(map_models, map_z), markers = 2 * n + seq_len(n) - 1))
}
contour_theme <- theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom",
                       panel.spacing.x = unit(1.4, "lines"), panel.grid = element_blank())
hit_band <- annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 0.05, ymax = 0.10, fill = NA, colour = "white",
                     linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dotted")
```

*Version `r crit_changelog$version[1]` (`r crit_changelog$date[1]`). See the [changelog](#crit-changelog).*

Since 1 October, a white crit in Forever gives **twice the rage of a normal hit**, and Dual Wield Specialization gives the off hand 50% more rage (see [the formula](#rage-formula)). Before that, a crit gave exactly the same rage as a normal hit, so this is the first time Forever's rage depends on anything your gear does other than how often you land a swing. ([How the Rules Changed](#crit-rework) tells how the rule got here, through two earlier versions.)

This chapter asks what the rule does for a Fury warrior in today's game. How much rage do you have, and how does it grow with crit, hit and attack power? Is there a ceiling? And does it change how the rotation *feels*, beyond the averages? We'll build it up from a single swing, compare it with Classic, and check our simulator against the community's rage spreadsheet.

## Our warrior

Our warrior is the one from the rest of the book: level 60, dual wielding a `r sprintf('%.1f', sim_defaults$mh_speed)` speed main hand and a `r sprintf('%.1f', sim_defaults$oh_speed)` speed off hand (both a phase 2-like weapon, `r crit_wpn` DPS), with the 17/34/0 Fury build the game launched with: Flurry 3/3 (`r pc0(forever_talents$flurry_haste)` attack speed), Improved Whirlwind and Reckless Swings, on top of Dual Wield Specialization, Furious Precision, Unbridled Wrath and Anger Management. What's different in this chapter:

- **The boss is level 63,** and we have no weapon skill from gear or race. Before any hit from gear, `r pc(0.27)` of white swings miss (it's high because dual wielding adds 19%), and `r pc(0.08)` of abilities do. `r pc(0.065)` are dodged, and `r pc(0.40)` of white swings are glancing blows, which do 55% to 75% damage (`r pc(forever_talents$glance_dmg)` on average, the same as Classic) and can't crit.
- **The boss takes `r pc(sim_defaults$crit_suppression)` off your crit,** as in wowsims: so 30% crit on your character sheet is about `r pc(0.30 - sim_defaults$crit_suppression)` against a boss. (This chapter used to assume no crit suppression, following Bored's spreadsheet and the tooltips; wowsims has it, and the book follows wowsims.)
- **Windfury Totem is always up** (a 20% chance of an extra main-hand swing, as in WarriorSim).
- **Gear is three numbers:** attack power from 1000 to 3000, crit on the character sheet from 15% to 45%, and hit from gear from 0% to 15%. Most warriors will have **5 to 10% hit**, and the plots mark that range.
- **Heroic Strike is queued at `r sim_defaults$hs_threshold` rage**, as in the rest of the book.

Each combination of gear is played in fights of `r crit_fight_len / 60` minutes: `r n_crit_ws` times in today's Forever, in wowsims, and `r n_crit` times in Classic, in our simulator (a simplified model, since wowsims only runs today's game). To see what the crit rule itself adds, we also play today's Forever with no crit bonus (a crit gives the same rage as a normal hit), with everything else the same. That one can't be run in wowsims, so it's played in our simulator, as Classic is.

*Today's Forever: `r crit_ws_stamp`.*

The Forever rage per swing comes from the combat logs shared by Tarch, Ryqenz (Zomd Aya), Siax, Budder, Ceece and elvenfresh. The attack table and Windfury follow GuybrushGit's [WarriorSim](https://github.com/GuybrushGit/WarriorSim). The check at the end of the chapter comes from Bored's [Forever rage spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vQLlq64gK7zXzv3HD5VRjT__BzzIiPwzu2zvz5JQtIJcKDU_Tskpd1M0Nf1r3NsM77hdR5-D_7xlpo9/pubhtml) (with thanks to Mikasax and Char). Everyone is credited in the [Contributors](#contributors) chapter.

## Step 1: one swing

In Forever, a swing that lands gives a fixed amount of rage for each second of weapon speed: about `r f2(forever_mh)` for the main hand and `r f2(forever_oh)` for the off hand (`r f2(forever_oh * forever_talents$oh_rage_mult)` with Dual Wield Specialization), whatever the swing's damage. So a `r sprintf('%.1f', sim_defaults$mh_speed)` speed main hand gives `r f1(forever_mh * sim_defaults$mh_speed)` rage a swing. Since a slower weapon also swings less often, the speed cancels out, and **each hand gives a fixed amount of rage per second**, as long as it lands.

The crit rule adds to that. Call $L$ the share of your swings that land, and $c$ the share that crit (every crit is a swing that lands, so $c$ is part of $L$). A crit gives $m = `r forever_talents$crit_rage_mult`$ times a normal swing's rage, so the rage of an average swing, as a share of a normal one, is

$$
\underbrace{L}_{\text{every landed swing}} \; + \; \underbrace{(m - 1)\,c}_{\text{the extra from crits}}
$$

With `r pc(0.30)` crit on your sheet (`r pc(0.30 - sim_defaults$crit_suppression)` against the boss) and `r pc(0.075)` hit, `r pc0(1 - (0.27 - 0.075) - 0.065)` of your main-hand swings land, so the crit bonus adds `r pc0((0.30 - sim_defaults$crit_suppression) / (1 - (0.27 - 0.075) - 0.065))` to your main hand's rage. Every extra 1% of crit adds about `r pc(0.01 / (1 - (0.27 - 0.075) - 0.065))` more.

This sum leaves out Flurry, Windfury, Unbridled Wrath and Reckless Swings, which the simulations include. Flurry matters here: more crits mean more Flurry, so more swings, and that rage grows with crit too, with or without the crit rule. Reckless Swings gives the same rage whatever your crit.

## Step 2: how much rage you have

Figure \@ref(fig:crit-lines) shows the full simulation, at `r pc(0.075)` hit, across every crit level. The dashed line is the `r bt_ww_need_now` rage per second that Bloodthirst and Whirlwind use when you press them on cooldown (from the [How Damage Scales chapter](#scaling)): below it, you can't keep both on cooldown, let alone Heroic Strike.

```{r crit-lines, fig.cap=paste0("Rage per second against crit, at 7.5% hit from gear, from the full fight simulation. Dark blue: today's Forever. Light blue: the same game with no crit bonus, so the gap between them is what the crit rule adds. Classic's rage depends on attack power, so it's shown at two levels. The dashed line is the ", bt_ww_need_now, " rage per second that Bloodthirst and Whirlwind use."), fig.height=4.8}
d <- bind_rows(
  crit_all %>% filter(model %in% c("Forever", "Forever, no crit bonus"), ap == 2000),
  crit_all %>% filter(model == "Classic", ap %in% c(1250, 2000)) %>% mutate(model = paste0("Classic (", ap, " AP)"))
) %>% filter(abs(hit - 0.075) < 1e-9)
ends <- d %>% filter(crit == max(crit))
ggplot(d, aes(crit, rps, colour = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = bt_ww_need_now, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.45, y = bt_ww_need_now, label = "Bloodthirst + Whirlwind", hjust = 1, vjust = 1.6, size = 3.2, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) + geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = ends, aes(label = model), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.01, direction = "y", size = 3.3,
                           segment.colour = "grey70", min.segment.length = 0, xlim = c(0.455, NA), show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = crit_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = pc, breaks = seq(0.15, 0.45, 0.05), limits = c(0.15, 0.58), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0))) +
  labs(x = "Crit (character sheet)", y = "Rage per second")
```

```{r}
tibble(pt = gear_points$point) %>%
  mutate(f = map_dbl(pt, ~ at_point("Forever", .x)), nb = map_dbl(pt, ~ at_point("Forever, no crit bonus", .x)),
         cl = map_dbl(pt, ~ at_point("Classic", .x)),
         sf = map_dbl(pt, ~ at_point("Forever", .x, "starved")), sc = map_dbl(pt, ~ at_point("Classic", .x, "starved"))) %>%
  transmute(Gear = map_chr(pt, gear_label), `Forever` = f2(f),
            `From the crit bonus` = sprintf("%s (%s)", f2(f - nb), pc0((f - nb) / f)),
            `Left after Bloodthirst and Whirlwind` = f2(f - bt_ww_need_now), Classic = f2(cl),
            `Time waiting for rage for Bloodthirst (Forever / Classic)` = paste(pc(sf), "/", pc(sc))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Rage per second at three gear points, in today's Forever and in Classic. The crit bonus column is what today's rule adds over a crit giving no extra rage, and its share of the total.")
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
f_all  <- crit_all %>% filter(model == "Forever", ap == 2000)
nb_all <- crit_all %>% filter(model == "Forever, no crit bonus")
bonus_share <- range(bonus_diff$d / bonus_diff$Forever)
cl_ap <- crit_all %>% filter(model == "Classic", abs(crit - 0.30) < 1e-9, abs(hit - 0.075) < 1e-9) %>% arrange(ap)
ap_cross <- approx(cl_ap$rps, cl_ap$ap, xout = gv("Forever", 0.30, 0.075))$y   # where Classic passes Forever
crit_gain <- function(m) gv(m, 0.45, 0.075) - gv(m, 0.15, 0.075)
hit_gain  <- function(m) gv(m, 0.30, 0.10) - gv(m, 0.30, 0)
```

What the simulation shows:

- **Today's Forever covers Bloodthirst and Whirlwind with any gear in our range.** Across the whole grid it has `r f2(min(f_all$rps))` to `r f2(max(f_all$rps))` rage per second, above the `r bt_ww_need_now` the two use, even with 15% crit and no hit. With no crit bonus it would fall a little short at the lowest gear (`r f2(min(nb_all$rps))`), so it's the crit rule that keeps both covered everywhere, on top of the high floor from Reckless Swings, Flurry and Dual Wield Specialization's off-hand bonus. Past that, the rage the crit rule adds goes to Heroic Strike.
- **The crit bonus is where the growth comes from.** It adds `r f2(min(bonus_diff$d))` to `r f2(max(bonus_diff$d))` rage per second across the grid. At 7.5% hit, going from 15% to 45% crit adds `r f2(crit_gain("Forever"))` rage per second, against `r f2(crit_gain("Forever, no crit bonus"))` with no crit bonus, which comes from Flurry alone.
- **Classic starts lower and ends higher.** Classic's rage grows with attack power as well as crit, so it starts well below Forever at early gear and passes it by late gear. At 30% crit and 7.5% hit, it passes Forever at about `r format(round(ap_cross, -2), big.mark = ",")` attack power. At early gear, a Classic warrior is waiting for rage for Bloodthirst `r pc(at_point("Classic", "Early", "starved"))` of the time, against `r pc(at_point("Forever", "Early", "starved"))` in Forever.

## Step 3: crit and hit together

Crit isn't the only thing that matters. Hit makes more of your swings land, and every swing that lands gives rage. Figure \@ref(fig:crit-contour) shows rage per second over every combination of the two, like a map where darker means more rage.

```{r crit-contour, fig.cap=paste0("Rage per second for every combination of crit and hit from gear, at 2000 attack power. Darker means more rage, and the thin white lines are steps of 0.5 rage per second. The white dotted box is 5 to 10% hit, where most warriors will be."), fig.height=4.8, fig.width=10}
d <- crit_all %>% filter(ap == 2000, model %in% main_models) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, main_models))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, aes(crit, hit)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = rps), interpolate = TRUE) +
  geom_contour(aes(z = rps), breaks = seq(5, 14, 0.5), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.7) +
  hit_band +
  facet_wrap(~ model, nrow = 1, labeller = as_labeller(crit_labs)) +
  rps_fill +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = pc, breaks = c(0.2, 0.3, 0.4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pc) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.15, 0.45), ylim = c(0, 0.15), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Crit (character sheet)", y = "Hit from gear") + contour_theme
```

```{r}
expand_grid(hit = c(0, 0.05, 0.075, 0.10), crit = c(0.15, 0.30, 0.45)) %>%
  mutate(v = f2(map2_dbl(crit, hit, ~ gv("Forever", .x, .y) - bt_ww_need_now)), crit = paste(pc0(crit), "crit"),
         `Hit from gear` = paste0(hit * 100, "%")) %>%
  select(-hit) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = crit, values_from = v) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Rage per second left for Heroic Strike in today's Forever, after the ", bt_ww_need_now, " that Bloodthirst and Whirlwind use, at 2000 attack power."))
```

With any gear in our range, you have rage to spare for Heroic Strike, and both stats add to it. At 30% crit, going from no hit to 10% adds `r f2(hit_gain("Forever"))` rage per second. At 7.5% hit, going from 15% to 45% crit adds `r f2(crit_gain("Forever"))`.

The crit rule doesn't make hit worth more, though. With no crit bonus, the same 10% of hit adds `r f2(hit_gain("Forever, no crit bonus"))`. That's the attack table: your crit chance is a share of *all* your swings, so more hit turns misses into normal hits, not into crits (until you reach the ceiling in Step 4).

Figure \@ref(fig:crit-map-pick) puts your own gear on the map. Set your crit and hit with the sliders: a red ring marks your gear on both maps, and the line above reads out your rage per second in each game.

```{r crit-map-pick, fig.cap=paste0("Figure \\@ref(fig:crit-contour) with your gear on it. Move the crit and hit sliders, and the red ring moves on both maps, while the line above reads out your rage per second in each game. At 2000 attack power."), out.width="100%", fig.height=5.5}
crit_map_pick()
```

## Step 4: attack power doesn't matter, and there's a ceiling

### Attack power

In Classic, rage came from damage, so attack power gave you rage too. In Forever, rage per swing doesn't depend on damage at all, and the crit rule doesn't change that: a crit gives twice the *rage* of a normal swing, not rage based on its damage. Figure \@ref(fig:crit-ap) shows it.

```{r crit-ap, fig.cap="Rage per second for every combination of attack power and crit, at 7.5% hit. In Forever, the colour and the thin white lines (steps of 0.5 rage per second) run straight across: going from 1000 to 3000 attack power changes nothing, and only crit moves your rage. In Classic, rage climbs with attack power as well as crit, because it comes from damage.", fig.height=4.8, fig.width=10}
d <- crit_all %>% filter(model %in% main_models, abs(hit - 0.075) < 1e-9) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, main_models))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, aes(ap, crit)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = rps), interpolate = TRUE) +
  geom_contour(aes(z = rps), breaks = seq(5, 14, 0.5), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ model, nrow = 1, labeller = as_labeller(crit_labs)) +
  rps_fill +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1500, 2000, 2500)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pc) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1000, 3000), ylim = c(0.15, 0.45), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Attack power", y = "Crit (character sheet)") + contour_theme
ap_spread <- crit_all %>% filter(model %in% main_models) %>% group_by(model, crit, hit) %>%
  summarise(s = max(rps) - min(rps), .groups = "drop") %>% group_by(model) %>% summarise(s = max(s))
```

Across the whole grid, attack power moves Forever's rage by `r f2(ap_spread$s[ap_spread$model == "Forever"])` rage per second, which is to say not at all, and Classic's by up to `r f1(ap_spread$s[ap_spread$model == "Classic"])`. This is why Forever's rage can't run away the way Classic's did: in Classic, every upgrade made you hit harder, which gave you more rage, which let you hit harder again. In Forever, only crit and hit can give you more rage, and both run into a ceiling.

### The ceiling

Every line in Figure \@ref(fig:crit-lines) flattens out after about 35 to 40% crit on the character sheet, Classic's included. At 7.5% hit, today's Forever gains `r f2(gv("Forever", 0.35, 0.075) - gv("Forever", 0.15, 0.075))` rage per second from 15% to 35% crit, and only `r f2(gv("Forever", 0.45, 0.075) - gv("Forever", 0.35, 0.075))` from 35% to 45%. That isn't a rule anyone wrote. It comes from the attack table.

Every white swing gets exactly one result from a single roll: a miss, a dodge, a glancing blow, a crit or a normal hit. Those shares have to add up to 100%. Against a level 63 boss, `r pc(0.40)` of white swings are glancing blows, which can't crit, so a white swing can crit at most

$$
c_{\max} \; = \; 1 \; - \; \text{miss} \; - \; \text{dodge} \; - \; \underbrace{0.40}_{\text{glancing}}
$$

of the time. Past that, more crit doesn't give a single extra crit on a white swing, so it gives no more rage either. Since the boss takes `r pc(sim_defaults$crit_suppression)` off your crit first, your character sheet reaches the ceiling at about `r pc(sim_defaults$crit_suppression)` above it.

```{r}
tibble(hit = c(0, 0.05, 0.075, 0.10, 0.15)) %>%
  transmute(`Hit from gear` = paste0(hit * 100, "%"), `Main hand` = pc(crit_cap(hit, "MH")), `Off hand` = pc(crit_cap(hit, "OH"))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "The most a white swing can crit against a level 63 boss, at each level of hit. The off hand has more room, because Furious Precision gives it 10% more hit.")
```

With `r pc(0.075)` hit, the main hand can't crit more than `r pc(crit_cap(0.075, "MH"))` of the time (about `r pc(crit_cap(0.075, "MH") + sim_defaults$crit_suppression)` on your character sheet), and the ceiling moves up with hit: every 1% of hit gives 1% more room for crits. So Forever's rage already has a cap. It's set by the attack table, not by the crit rule, and it sits near the top of the gear we expect.

## Step 5: how it feels

Averages hide something every Fury warrior knows: rage comes in streaks. You can get four Heroic Strikes in a row, then none for a minute. Heroic Strikes per minute can't tell those two apart, so we'll look at the **time between one Heroic Strike and the next**. (The *average* time between them is just 60 divided by the number per minute, so it tells us nothing new. What we need is how spread out those waits are.)

We'll use one number for the bad streaks: the **1-in-10 wait**, the wait that 1 in 10 gaps between Heroic Strikes is longer than. If it's 20 seconds, then 9 times out of 10, your next Heroic Strike comes within 20 seconds of the last one.

```{r crit-p90, fig.cap="The long waits: 1 in 10 gaps between Heroic Strikes is longer than this, for every combination of crit and hit, at 2000 attack power. Darker means longer droughts (waits of 60 seconds or more all share the darkest colour).", fig.height=4.8, fig.width=10}
d <- crit_all %>% filter(ap == 2000, model %in% main_models) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, main_models), gap_p90 = pmin(gap_p90, 60))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, aes(crit, hit)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = gap_p90), interpolate = TRUE) +
  hit_band +
  facet_wrap(~ model, nrow = 1, labeller = as_labeller(crit_labs)) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#fee6ce", "#fdae6b", "#fd8d3c", "#d94801", "#7f2704"), limits = c(0, 60),
                       breaks = seq(0, 60, 15), labels = c(seq(0, 45, 15), "60 or more"),
                       name = "Seconds (1 in 10 waits is longer than this)",
                       guide = guide_colourbar(barwidth = unit(14, "lines"), title.position = "top")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = pc, breaks = c(0.2, 0.3, 0.4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pc) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.15, 0.45), ylim = c(0, 0.15), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Crit (character sheet)", y = "Hit from gear") + contour_theme
```

Figure \@ref(fig:crit-p90-3d) shows the same thing in 3D, with attack power on the slider. Here the height and colour are the 1-in-10 wait, so higher and darker is worse, and the contour lines underneath are steps of 10 seconds. Forever's waits don't change with attack power, but Classic's fall as attack power climbs, because more damage means more rage.

```{r crit-p90-3d, fig.cap="The 1-in-10 wait between Heroic Strikes (height and colour, capped at 120 seconds) by crit and hit (the floor), with attack power on the slider, in each game. Higher and darker is a longer drought.", out.width="100%", fig.height=6}
crit3d("gap_p90", "1-in-10 wait (sec)", colours = c("#fee6ce", "#fdae6b", "#fd8d3c", "#d94801", "#7f2704"),
       cmin = 0, cmax = 120, step = 10, zcap = 120, fmt = ".0f", unit = " sec")
```

Figure \@ref(fig:crit-wait) zooms in on our three gear points. Each line shows how likely it is that your next Heroic Strike has come within a given number of seconds of the last one.

```{r crit-wait, fig.cap="How long until your next Heroic Strike, at three gear points. Each line is the chance that the next Heroic Strike has gone off within x seconds of the last one: higher and further left is steadier. Where a line crosses the dotted line, 9 in 10 waits are shorter than that.", fig.height=5, fig.width=10}
wait_models <- c("Forever", "Forever, no crit bonus", "Classic")
d <- expand_grid(pt = gear_points$point, model = wait_models) %>%
  mutate(curves = map2(pt, model, function(p, m) {
    g <- gaps_at(m, p); x <- seq(0, 120, 0.5); tibble(x = x, share = map_dbl(x, ~ mean(g <= .x)))
  })) %>% unnest(curves) %>%
  mutate(label = factor(map_chr(pt, gear_label), map_chr(gear_points$point, gear_label)), model = factor(model, wait_models))
ggplot(d, aes(x, share, colour = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.9, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = crit_cols, labels = crit_labs, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pc, limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.04))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 30, 60, 90), limits = c(0, 120), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(x = "Seconds since the last Heroic Strike", y = "Chance the next one has come by now") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.spacing.x = unit(1.4, "lines"), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

```{r}
expand_grid(pt = gear_points$point, Rules = wait_models) %>%
  mutate(hs = map2_dbl(Rules, pt, ~ at_point(.x, .y, "hs")), med = map2_dbl(Rules, pt, ~ at_point(.x, .y, "gap_med")),
         p90 = map2_dbl(Rules, pt, ~ at_point(.x, .y, "gap_p90"))) %>%
  transmute(Gear = pt, Rules = recode(Rules, Forever = "Forever today", `Forever, no crit bonus` = "Forever today, no crit bonus"),
            `Heroic Strikes per minute` = f1(hs), `Typical wait (median)` = paste(f0(med), "sec"),
            `1-in-10 wait` = paste(f0(p90), "sec")) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Heroic Strikes and the waits between them at the three gear points.")
```

What stands out:

- **The crit bonus makes rage steadier.** With no crit bonus, today's Forever would Heroic Strike `r f1(at_point("Forever, no crit bonus", "Mid", "hs"))` times a minute at mid gear, and 1 in 10 waits would be longer than `r f0(at_point("Forever, no crit bonus", "Mid", "gap_p90"))` seconds. With it, that's `r f1(at_point("Forever", "Mid", "hs"))` times a minute and `r f0(at_point("Forever", "Mid", "gap_p90"))` seconds. More rage means shorter droughts.
- **Forever is much steadier than Classic at early gear.** 1 in 10 waits is longer than `r f0(at_point("Forever", "Early", "gap_p90"))` seconds in Forever, against `r f0(at_point("Classic", "Early", "gap_p90"))` in Classic. By mid gear the two are about the same (`r f0(at_point("Forever", "Mid", "gap_p90"))` and `r f0(at_point("Classic", "Mid", "gap_p90"))` seconds). At late gear Classic is a little steadier (`r f0(at_point("Classic", "Late", "gap_p90"))` against `r f0(at_point("Forever", "Late", "gap_p90"))`), because at high attack power it's queueing Heroic Strike almost every swing.

## Checking our simulator against Bored's spreadsheet

Bored's [Forever rage spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vQLlq64gK7zXzv3HD5VRjT__BzzIiPwzu2zvz5JQtIJcKDU_Tskpd1M0Nf1r3NsM77hdR5-D_7xlpo9/pubhtml), which the community uses to plan rage, added the 30 September rule (crits give 75% more rage) that day. It works out rage per second with a formula, where we play out fights, so the two make a good check on each other. The spreadsheet's formula, for each hand, is

$$
\text{base rage} \times (1 + 0.75\,\text{crit}) \times (1 - \text{miss} - \text{dodge}) \times \text{attack speed} \times \text{Windfury},
$$

plus Unbridled Wrath. Our version of that formula matches every row of the spreadsheet. Our simulator, given the spreadsheet's assumptions and no Heroic Strike, comes out close to it, and a little above at high crit (the last paragraph of this section explains why). The other differences come from the assumptions, and Table \@ref(tab:crit-sheet) swaps them for ours one at a time. (The spreadsheet models the 30 September rule on the 1 October build, so this check uses that rule too. [How the Rules Changed](#crit-rework) has the rule versions.)

```{r crit-sheet}
sheet_res %>% mutate(step = factor(step, names(sheet_steps))) %>% select(row, step, rps) %>%
  mutate(rps = f2(rps)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = row, values_from = rps) %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(step = "The spreadsheet", !!!setNames(as.list(sprintf("%.2f", sheet_rows$sheet_rps)), sheet_rows$row)), .) %>%
  rename(` ` = step) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Rage per second in Bored's spreadsheet, and in our simulator as we swap the spreadsheet's assumptions for ours one at a time (each row keeps the changes above it).")
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
sr <- function(step, row) sheet_res$rps[sheet_res$step == step & sheet_res$row == sheet_rows$row[row]]
st <- names(sheet_steps)
step_gap <- function(a, b, row) sr(st[b], row) - sr(st[a], row)
```

- **Heroic Strike** makes the biggest difference, and more the better your gear (`r f1(step_gap(1, 2, 1))` rage per second in the first column, `r f1(step_gap(1, 2, 4))` in the last). In Forever, Heroic Strike replaces a white swing, and that swing's rage is lost. The spreadsheet counts that as part of Heroic Strike's cost (22 rage each, not 12), where we count it as rage you never got. Both are right; they just book it in different places.
- **Anger Management**, which we include and the spreadsheet leaves out (it notes it's worth 20 rage a minute): `r sprintf("%+.1f", step_gap(5, 6, 1))` rage per second.
- **The extra 3% attack speed** from enchants, which the spreadsheet includes and we don't: about `r sprintf("%+.1f", mean(map_dbl(1:4, ~ step_gap(3, 4, .x))))` rage per second.
- **Windfury's cooldown, the miss table** (the tooltips' 27.6% white miss against our 27%) **and the off hand's speed** each move it by less than 0.1.

So at low gear, our assumptions land almost exactly on the spreadsheet (`r f2(sr(st[7], 1))` against `r sprintf("%.2f", sheet_rows$sheet_rps[1])`), with Anger Management making up for the attack speed. At high gear we come out lower, almost all of it from Heroic Strike.

Two smaller things in the spreadsheet are worth knowing about. It applies the crit bonus only to swings that land, but on the attack table, crit is a share of *all* swings, so it undercounts crit rage a little. That's why our simulator, with the spreadsheet's assumptions, comes out a little above it at high crit. And it takes Flurry as up 80% of the time, where in the simulation Flurry's uptime grows with crit (well below 80% at 25% crit, about 80% at 45%). Neither changes the picture.

## Where the numbers come from

- **Announced:** the crit bonus (twice a normal swing's rage, in both hands), Dual Wield Specialization's +50% off-hand rage, Furious Precision's off-hand hit, and the 2 November talents (Flurry's 30%, Improved Whirlwind and Reckless Swings).
- **Measured:** the rage per swing for each hand, that it doesn't depend on damage, and that a hasted swing gives the full rage (the [Rage Generation chapter](#rage)).
- **From wowsims:** today's Forever at every gear point, including the Heroic Strike waits (from its combat logs), the attack table against a level 63 boss with its crit suppression, and what Windfury Totem's strike gives.
- **Assumed:** Windfury itself, since it needs a shaman in the group.
- **Our guesses:** the gear ranges, and the rotation, with Heroic Strike queued at `r sim_defaults$hs_threshold` rage.

The most useful logs for this chapter would come from level 60 dual wielders, with their gear posted, to replace our guessed gear ranges with real ones.

## Conclusion

1. **Crit is Forever's rage stat now.** A crit gives twice a normal swing's rage, which adds `r f2(min(bonus_diff$d))` to `r f2(max(bonus_diff$d))` rage per second across our gear range, `r pc0(bonus_share[1])` to `r pc0(bonus_share[2])` of the total. Without the rule, crit would only add rage through Flurry.
2. **Any gear covers Bloodthirst and Whirlwind.** Today's warrior has at least `r f2(min(f_all$rps))` rage per second in our grid, against the `r bt_ww_need_now` the two use. Reckless Swings, Flurry and the off-hand bonus nearly cover them on their own, so the crit bonus goes to Heroic Strike.
3. **Hit gives rage, but the crit rule doesn't make it worth more.** It turns misses into normal hits, not into crits.
4. **Attack power still gives no rage**, so Forever's rage can't run away like Classic's did. Forever starts ahead of Classic, and Classic passes it at about `r format(round(ap_cross, -2), big.mark = ",")` attack power (at 30% crit and 7.5% hit).
5. **There's already a ceiling.** A white swing can't crit more than the attack table leaves room for (about `r pc(crit_cap(0.075, "MH"))` for the main hand at 7.5% hit, or `r pc(crit_cap(0.075, "MH") + sim_defaults$crit_suppression)` on the character sheet), so rage flattens out after about 35 to 40% crit.
6. **The crit bonus makes the rotation steadier.** At mid gear, the 1-in-10 wait between Heroic Strikes is `r f0(at_point("Forever", "Mid", "gap_p90"))` seconds, against `r f0(at_point("Forever, no crit bonus", "Mid", "gap_p90"))` with no crit bonus. At early gear, Forever is much steadier than Classic.

Today's Forever comes from wowsims, which follows the game's rules; Classic and the no-crit-bonus line come from our simplified simulator. The gear ranges are our guesses, so the exact numbers are there to illustrate what's happening, not to predict your own. The shapes are the part to take away.
